articles.title: PCB supply risks may rival chip shortages, threatening next wave of AI and electronics growth
articles.short_snippet: The Global Electronics Association says shortages across the printed circuit board supply chain are intensifying, with companies in the automotive, industrial, medical, and telecommunications sectors reporting that surging AI demand is consuming limited capacity. articles.title: Nvidia's Southeast Asia shipment freeze tests Taiwan's AI-server manufacturing hedge

articles.title: Samsung, SK Hynix pursue different DRAM designs
articles.short_snippet: Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix are pursuing different approaches to increasing DRAM density as the capacitors used to store data become harder to shrink. Samsung is developing vertically stacked memory cells, while SK Hynix is testing a design that eliminates the capacitor altogether.

articles.title: Samsung hesitates to take on Nvidia in robot chips
articles.short_snippet: South Korea asked Samsung Electronics in October to develop a domestic alternative to Nvidia's Jetson Thor robotics computing platform, but the chipmaker expressed reservations over market demand, South Korean broadcaster MTN reported, citing a government official.

articles.title: LG AI Research targets data and model bottlenecks in smart manufacturing
articles.short_snippet: LG AI Research is automating data preparation, building expert foundation models, and setting up an autonomous laboratory to ease the burden on companies that want to deploy AI and keep using it, particularly in manufacturing.

articles.title: GenAI fails to spur upgrades as smartphone shipments face 2027 decline
articles.short_snippet: Rising memory prices are expected to drive a more than 15% decline in global smartphone shipments in 2026. With memory costs continuing to rise, brands reducing their midrange and entry-level models, and consumers delaying upgrades, a research firm expects global smartphone shipments to fall another 6% in 2027.

articles.title: Alpha Networks to ship 1.6T switches in small volumes in December
articles.short_snippet: Alpha Networks plans to begin small-volume shipments of its 1.6T switch products in December 2026 and is targeting large data center customers to expand shipments in 2027. Some equipment that was due this year has been pushed back to next year.

articles.title: Global smartphone shipments to fall a further 6% in 2027 as memory squeeze persists

articles.title: DIGITIMES Insight: KV cache growth will not translate one-for-one into CXL memory demand

CXL becomes necessary only when host DRAM is constrained, the data is worth reusing, and the service depends on reloading it quickly.
